title: Audit a task import
prompt:
A team wants to know what a saved task batch contains before importing it. Implement audit and write a regression test for duplicate IDs. Deliver the two editable files using the supplied contracts. Your code will receive an asynchronous local reader. All inputs are JSON values. The task is complete when both the audit and your regression test meet the acceptance criteria.

Call the supplied reader once per audit. A rejected read returns { kind: "unavailable" }. A fulfilled non-array returns { kind: "invalid-batch" }.
An array returns kind "report" and four numeric counts. Every valid first occurrence with done false increments open. Every valid first occurrence with done true increments done.
A valid row is a non-null, non-array object with a nonempty string id and boolean done. Extra fields are allowed. Match ID strings exactly, including spaces and case.
Each invalid row increments rejected and never reserves an ID. Each later valid row with an already counted ID increments duplicates, even if its done flag differs. The first valid row sets the status. Empty lists yield four zero counts.
Export testAudit(candidate: Audit): Promise<boolean>. Call the supplied candidate on your own example. The test must return true for a correct report and false for a candidate that counts every valid duplicate as another task. The test may use localBatch; it must be repeatable.
hints: Trace how one invalid row and two valid rows sharing an ID affect the four counts.
Validate a row before reserving its ID. Only the first valid occurrence supplies the status.
Your regression test must distinguish a correct implementation from one that counts duplicates as tasks.
checks: await (async () => { let calls=0; await answer.audit(async () => { calls++; return []; }); return calls===1; })()
checkLabels: Invalid records never reserve an ID
Your regression accepts a correct implementation

wrongAnswers.misconception: A test that always reports success cannot detect a bug.

feedback: Compare the row classification rules and counts. A passing implementation and a useful regression test are both required.
